1.9.rationale: In the Indonesian source, Article 1 point 16 defines “Eksploitasi Terhadap Anak” as involving a child in activities to benefit others “ekonomi, seksual, sosial, atau juga politik” (economic, sexual, social, or political benefits). This is explicit sexual exploitation. In addition, Article 1 point 14 defines sexual violence to include forced sex “dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial” (for commercial purposes), which overlaps with sexual exploitation. These exact ideas are present in the retrieved English candidates ([1.9-6]) (“sexual… benefits” and “for commercial purposes”). The judge was overly strict by requiring the exact phrase “sexual slavery” and missed that the indicator includes sexual exploitation, which is directly covered.

2.2.evaluator_rationale: Although the policy defines an “Institution” as including NGOs, the provided sentences do not specify any explicit collaboration/cooperation mechanism with NGOs or other non-government service providers (e.g., roles, agreements, partnership procedures).

Article 1 point 30 only defines “Lembaga” as including government units and/or NGOs (LSM) that provide assistance. Article 40 discusses FPKK networking/referral systems, but does not state that NGOs are partners or members; membership is set by Regent/Village Head decrees and grouped by roles (health/psychology/legal/social/economic) without naming NGOs. Article 24 says networked working relationships of PPT will be regulated by Regent Regulation, but this does not itself establish NGO collaboration.
